summary: WinUI 3 migration structurally reproduces all 6 UWP scenarios (verbatim nav titles, Register/Unregister buttons, Status output, correct default enabled/disabled states), verified element-by-element via the UIA tree. No missing controls, no dropped scenarios. Parity gate: PASS 100/100. Remaining items are environment/measurement limitations, not demonstrated migration defects.

items.detail: All WinUI 3 screenshots captured blank (11273 bytes) because the WinUI 3 DirectComposition surface does not render into PrintWindow-based captures in this non-interactive/headless session. The UIA tree confirms full, correct content is present (6 nav items, Description, Register/Unregister buttons, Status). The UWP CoreWindow, by contrast, did render, so its launch frame is non-blank. This is a capture-environment artifact, not a blank/crashed page.

Register/Unregister could not be actuated on either app. WinUI 3: the enabled, on-screen Button exposes no InvokePattern through its automation peer in this environment, and synthetic mouse/foreground input is unavailable in the non-interactive session (SetCursorPos/SetForegroundWindow are no-ops). UWP: the CoreWindow exposes an empty UIA subtree and the same input synthesis is unavailable. Register is additionally permission-gated via BackgroundExecutionManager.RequestAccessAsync(). Per the parity rule, an un-actuatable control with no UWP behavioral golden is flagged for manual review, not failed. No behavioral regression was demonstrated.

Per-scenario UWP golden navigation was not automatable (empty CoreWindow UIA subtree + no synthetic input). The mandatory hard gate is satisfied: the original UWP app launched (ok:true) and the live launch frame documents all six scenarios in the nav and scenario 1's full content as ground truth. Per-scenario UWP baseline frames beyond the launch frame were therefore not captured.

Extract-UwpFeatureChecklist found 0 interactive controls per scenario because the scenario .xaml files are absent from the standalone UWP source (only .xaml.cs present); it captured the shared Status output. The actual Register/Unregister buttons were verified directly against the running UWP app and the migrated WinUI 3 UIA tree.
